evidence.quote: Jan Anthonie Coxie or Anthonie Coxie ( c . 1660 - 1720 )

events.label: career
events.text: Began his career in Mechelen, around 1691.

evidence.quote: Jan Anthonie commenced his career in Mechelen around the year 1691

events.text: Commissioned by Mechelen to paint portrait of Charles II of Spain.

evidence.quote: That year he was commissioned by the city of Mechelen to make a portrait of Charles II of Spain

events.text: Painted Group Portrait of the FaydHerbe Family in an Architectural Setting.

evidence.quote: Group Portrait of the FaydHerbe Family in an Architectural Setting ( in a private collection ) of 1693

events.text: Painted the figures in a landscape by Jacques d'Arthois for St. James Church, Bruges.

evidence.quote: In 1698 he painted the figures in a landscape made by Jacques dArthois for the St . James Church in Bruges

events.text: Recorded as living and working in Amsterdam from 1699.

evidence.quote: From 1699 onwards he is recorded in Amsterdam
In 1703 he became poorter of Amsterdam
he left Amsterdam and is recorded in Berlin from 1705 to 1708

events.text: Recorded in Berlin from 1705, serving Frederick I of Prussia.

evidence.quote: he left Amsterdam and is recorded in Berlin from 1705 to 1708
is recorded in Berlin from 1705 to 1708

events.text: Left Berlin for Mainz, where he worked for the court.

evidence.quote: After the death of his patron , Coxie left Berlin for Mainz in 1713
He did not stay in Mainz for long but moved around 1713 to Milan
until his death , probably in Milan , in 1720

undated_mentions: Studied with his father Jan Coxie and with Charles Emmanuel Biset (education)
Born in Mechelen, some time between 1650 and 1670 (exact year unknown)
Became court painter of Frederick I of Prussia in Berlin
Decorated ceilings of Charlottenburg Palace and Berlin Palace for Frederick I
Painted walls and altarpiece in the Chapel at Charlottenburg Palace
Porcelain room ceiling frescos for Charlottenburg Palace (Berlin period)
Worked for the court in Mainz
Wybrand de Geest became his pupil
Amsterdam-period portraits of Nicolaas van der Meer and Antoni de Mestral
